framework: 3-Step Hook: Context Lean -> Scroll-Stop -> Contrarian Snapback
observed_evidence: Thomas 1.0M opening: frame (fall prevention) -> stop ('not something you buy, not install, not a new routine') -> snapback ('a change in how you walk'); Ares 351K: 2:47 a.m. scene -> 'bladder has almost nothing to do with it'
counterexample: b8uLzWR-ZGo uses the same 'what if... not coming from your knee' snapback and got 2.5K

framework: Intro Analyzer: judge first 0-30 s for clarity/curiosity/emotion
observed_evidence: Hook archetype medians (within-channel multiple): DIRECT_COMMAND 1.65x, WHAT_IF 1.30x, WARNING 0.32x (14/22 below 0.5x)
counterexample: Pair 20: two DIRECT_COMMAND openings one day apart -> 1,133 vs 32
result: PARTIALLY_SUPPORTED (archetype explains little on its own)

framework: Packaging SOP: know the audience, bold big text, fewer words, one big idea
observed_evidence: Answer-withheld thumbnails 1.90x vs revealed 0.47x (0/14 revealed >=3x); <=8 words 1.19x vs 0.95x; clutter (high bg complexity) 0.91x vs 1.16x
result: SUPPORTED (one-big-idea + withheld answer); word-count rule weak

videos_tested_against: Cannot test - no retention/traffic data (first-party analytics absent)

framework: Viral Checklist: name a specific audience pain point
observed_evidence: Winners open on a pain the viewer already has (numb feet, nightly bathroom trips, 'one pill every day'); losers open on invisible conditions (silent kidney decline) or jargon (beta blockers)
counterexample: Pair 11: loser opens on a vivid pain story (Olivia's numb hand) and still fails

observed_evidence: Thumbnail large number 2.13x vs 0.80x; Aliza 4-drug roll-call 47K vs single drug 31
counterexample: Thomas knee video: stat-dense (64%, 1,100 adults) -> 2.5K; title has_specificity regex 0.88x
result: PARTIALLY_SUPPORTED (concrete numbers help; unverifiable stats do not)

videos_tested_against: Title has_contrarian (n=13) 1.94x; Okoro 'Medical tests that may be unnecessary' 8.0x; TopHealthTips 'Walking Won't Make Your Legs Stronger' 800K
counterexample: 'Stop walking' (SHH 352) and 'Magnesium pills are useless' (1.5K) - contrarian + inaccurate fails

framework: Title Analyzer: 7 viral title formulas framed against viewer satisfaction
observed_evidence: Identical formula titles range 2 views to 1.6M across channels
counterexample: Same title, same week: Ares 1.47M vs Elias 28K (sleeping position)

framework: 16 Commandments: promise alignment (title promise delivered by script)
observed_evidence: Okoro delivers all 9 promised signs (~250 words each); clove video delivers a timeline but title '10 minutes' vs script '15 minutes' mismatch
counterexample: Clove video still 3.09M despite mismatch - promise alignment not required for views (may matter for satisfaction, unmeasured)

framework: BUT/THEREFORE causal chaining instead of 'and then'
observed_evidence: Okoro: 'Walter felt fine... BUT numb feet... THEREFORE one extra test -> A1C 9.2'. Clove: 'coffee is healthy BUT sugar/milk cancel it THEREFORE brew with clove'
counterexample: Pattern-interrupt lexicon ('but here's') density does not separate winners from losers (0.0-1.8/1k in both)

framework: Creative Engine / Script Analyzer: narrative spine + retention mechanics + CTA alignment
observed_evidence: Winners more often place an open loop in the first ~100 s (Okoro 96s, Aliza 11s, Ares 81s) and a bridge to a related video at the end (Okoro kidney -> foot breakout)
counterexample: Pair 5: winner has no open loop detected; pair 8 loser has no loop and no enumeration

observed_evidence: Ares/Elias sketch-illustration template and SHH 3D organ renders are consistent with AI-generated imagery (not verified)

framework: Video SEO checklist (keyword research, tags, description)
observed_evidence: Several large winners had near-zero web search demand (bathing: 0/100 before upload; best fruit for eyes: 0 in upload week)
counterexample: Neuropathy exercises winner aligned with a search peak (GT-24)
result: WEAK for this niche (discovery appears browse/suggested-led; traffic data UNKNOWN)
